steps.subject: Your Perpline account is ready
steps.preheader: Compare exchanges side by side before you sign up anywhere.
steps.headline: Welcome to Perpline
steps.body:
Your account is set up. Perpline lists centralized exchanges and perp DEXs side by side so you can compare trading fees and referral terms before you open an account.

Perpline is not available to residents of South Korea or the United States.

You can manage your account and email preferences at any time.

steps.label: GUIDE · 02
steps.subject: How fee rebates actually work
steps.preheader: A short explainer before you pick an exchange.
steps.headline:
Where a rebate
comes from
steps.body:
When you sign up through a referral link, the exchange shares part of the trading fee it charges you. Some programs pass a portion back to you as a rebate or a fee discount.

Terms differ by exchange and can change, so always check the current terms on the exchange itself before you trade.

Futures and perpetual contracts are high-risk products and you can lose more than your initial margin.

steps.label: GUIDE · 03
steps.subject: CEX or perp DEX? A two-minute checklist
steps.preheader: Custody, KYC, liquidity and fees — what to weigh.
steps.headline: CEX or perp DEX?
steps.body:
Four questions worth asking before you choose:

Custody. Do you want the exchange to hold your funds, or keep them in your own wallet?
Verification. Are you comfortable with KYC?
Liquidity. Is the order book deep enough for your size?
Fees. What do you pay as maker and as taker?

Perpline keeps both lists on one page so you can check each answer quickly.

Not investment advice. Futures trading carries a high risk of loss.
